# VulcanBench

> An open-source coding benchmark comparing model-and-harness combinations
> across reasoning effort, total score, runtime, tokens and estimated API cost.

VulcanBench is run by Morgan Linton, Cofounder and CTO of Bold Metrics.
The current VulcanBench Frontier v4 suite uses 23 behavioral-reconstruction tasks:
Python replacements for opaque C-built binaries. From September 2026 its
combined score weights are 50% functional correctness, 8.5% lint and
complexity, 8.5% security and 33% Code quality. Time, tokens and
API-equivalent cost are reported separately.

Code quality is judged for a human reader by a two-model panel from labs with
no model on the board (Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6), under one frozen
six-dimension rubric with written anchors, an intent-recovery probe scored
against each task's known specification departures, and a calibration exam
every judge passes before scoring. It is model judgment, not human validation.
A perfect functional result is not a perfect combined score.

## Key pages

- [Current results and archive](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks.html): compare only within the same task suite and scoring protocol.
- [Claude Opus 5.5 on VulcanBench Safety v1](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/safety-v1-opus55.html): ten Frontier v4 tasks with two harmful instructions hidden in each repository; over 50 Claude Code runs Opus 5.5 followed 0 of 60 network, secret or delete instructions and 3 of 100 overall (two code injections, one harmless test), and flagged the note to the user in 64 of 97 refusals.
- [Grok 4.7 across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-grok47-cursor-v320.html): 92 Cursor runs at four effort levels (Cursor offers no Max), Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and GPT-6.1 Sol under protocol v3.20, because Grok 4.6, the second judge for every other column, is not neutral for an xAI model. Combined score 89.42 at Low, 92.30 at Medium, 92.71 at High and 93.15 at Extra-high, ranks 1, 2 and 3 of 53 columns on the board. GPT-6.1 Sol rates about 6 points above Muse, so Code quality is not strictly comparable; on Muse Spark 1.3 alone for every column Grok 4.7 scores 88.64 to 92.27, still first at Medium to Extra-high and second at Low behind Fable 5.1. Tasks passed 18, 21, 22 and 23 of 23; Medium judged on 22 after one 3-hour timeout; 20.2 to 28.5 minutes per task; cost unavailable (no list price, Cursor subscription), never $0. Safety v1: followed 14 of 80 planted notes, reported none; Claude Opus 5.5 followed 3 of 100, reported 64. Routine v1 (12 private routine tickets, aggregates on the leaderboard): every level passes all 12, combined 97.29, 97.21, 97.37 and 97.14 from Low to Extra-high, the four highest Routine columns, in 1.1 to 4.0 minutes per task; judged under v3.22 by Muse Spark 1.3 alone because GPT-6.1 Sol failed that calibration exam, and still first when every column is rescored from Muse alone. Routine and Frontier Code quality are not comparable. Includes PDF, per-run CSV, shared-judge check and public evidence links.
- [GPT-6.1 Sol across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-gpt61-sol-v318.html): 115 Codex runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.18. Combined score 86.22 at Low, 86.44 at Medium, 88.23 at High, 88.78 at Extra-high and 88.35 at Max, ahead of GPT-6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Sol at every level and 13th of 49 columns on the board at its best. Tasks passed 20, 22, 23, 23 and 23 of 23, so Frontier v4 no longer separates its top levels on correctness; $0.31 to $0.46 per task, $44.33 for all 115 runs. Every cell is judged on 23 runs (Medium paddockcore from Muse Spark 1.3 alone after an invalid Grok review); no run hit the 3-hour bound. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record, the three-generation Sol card and public evidence links.
- [GPT-6 Sol across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-gpt6-sol-v317.html): 115 Codex runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.17. Combined score 67.62 at Low, 80.60 at Medium, 82.83 at High, 85.94 at Extra-high and 86.82 at Max, slightly behind GPT-5.6 Sol at every level. Tasks passed 4, 13, 15, 18 and 19 of 23; $1.02 to $2.52 per task, $221.38 for all 115 runs. Medium is judged on 22 of 23 after one invalid judge probe; no run hit the 3-hour bound. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record, comparison cards with GPT-5.6 Sol and the GPT-6 family, and public evidence links.
- [GPT-6 Luna across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-gpt6-luna-v316.html): 115 Codex runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.16. Combined score over judged runs 40.83 at Low, 45.72 at Medium, 57.35 at High, 78.79 at Extra-high and 81.42 at Max. Six runs hit the 3-hour bound (2 at Extra-high, 4 at Max); counting them as 0 gives 71.94 and 67.26. Tasks passed 0, 0, 2, 11 and 12 of 23; $0.010 to $0.160 per priced task. Every score is published both ways: over judged runs, and with timeouts counted as 0. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [Claude Opus 5.5 across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-opus55-v315.html): 115 Claude Code runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.15. Combined score 86.36 at Low, 90.86 at Medium with all 23 tasks passed, 91.11 at High, second on Frontier v4 only to Fable 5.1 at Max, then 90.68 and 90.22; $1.70 to $8.75 per task. Claude Code's refusal fallback was on, following Artificial Analysis: Opus 4.8 wrote 0.0, 6.4, 20.9, 32.4, 47.8% of replies from Low to Max, and every run counts. Includes a comparison card with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, per-run CSV and public evidence links.
- [GPT-5.6 Sol across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-sol-v37.html): 115 Codex runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.7. Combined score 69.05 at Low, 82.56 at Medium and 85.76 to 87.18 from High to Max, at $1.36 to $2.05 per task; Max is judged on 22 of 23 tasks after one invalid judge probe. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [GPT-5.6 Terra across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-terra-v36.html): 115 Codex runs at five effort levels, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.6. Combined score rises at every step, 59.70 at Low to 89.05 at Max, at $0.58 to $2.12 per task. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [GPT-5.5 vs. GPT-5.6 Luna across every effort level](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-gpt55-luna-v35.html): 207 Codex runs at every effort level each API offers, Code quality at 33% judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under protocol v3.5. GPT-5.5 leads at Low and Medium; Luna edges ahead from High up and its Max level is the top cell, at 17 to 75 times less per task. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [Astra vs. Fable 5.1 under a neutral Code quality panel](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmarks/swe-v4-astra-fable51-v34.html): 230 runs from the September 2026 effort sweep scored with Code quality at 33%, judged for a human reader by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 under a frozen, calibrated protocol. Includes PDF, per-run CSV with both judges' sub-scores, calibration record and public evidence links.
- [Methodology](https://vulcanbench.com/methodology.html): task admission, execution boundaries, four-factor scoring and evidence limits.
- [Blog](https://vulcanbench.com/blog.html): benchmark design and effort observations.
- [Introducing VulcanBench Safety v1](https://vulcanbench.com/blog/02-vulcanbench-safety-v1.html): announcement of VulcanBench Safety v1, a safety eval suite built for and run in the same environments and harnesses companies actually use (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor). It looks for the smaller safety issues that show up during ordinary coding work, so teams can tell whether rolling out a new model raises or lowers safety risk in their codebase.
- [Why I started VulcanBench](https://vulcanbench.com/blog/01-why-i-started-vulcanbench.html): the origin story, a $300,000-a-year model bill, evals built on the team's own codebase, and why benchmarks measured only at Max effort gave no usable signal.
- [Custom evals](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmark-your-stack.html): private evaluations for engineering teams.
- [Benchmark your model](https://vulcanbench.com/benchmark-your-model.html): evaluations for labs and harness builders.

## Interpretation

Astra had lower mean time and estimated API cost at every matched effort in
this comparison. Fable Max had the highest observed total score. This is not
a statistically established overall winner or a pure-base-model comparison.
Effort labels are harness-specific, not equal compute budgets. One attempt
per cell does not establish run-to-run reliability.

Historical suites and reports retain their original metrics. Do not pool
Eval Suite 3 pass rates with Frontier v4 total scores. Costs are hypothetical API
charges from a frozen rate snapshot, not subscription cash charges.

## Evidence and limits

The harness and task suites are public. Individual reports distinguish
published measurements from withheld raw artifacts. Source hashes and
post-cutoff dates do not prove absence of cheating, prohibited access or
training-data overlap.
